All three carry semantics; they differ in the kind of emphasis:

html
<p><strong>Warning:</strong> do not power off during the update.</p>
<p>I did <em>not</em> say he took the money.</p>   <!-- shifts stress, shifts meaning -->
<p>Results for "react": Learn <mark>React</mark> from scratch</p>
ElementMeaningDefault look
<strong>high importancebold
<em>stress emphasis that changes the sentenceitalic
<mark>relevant to the current context (search term)yellow highlight

Their counterparts <b> and <i> change appearance only, with no meaning. Use <i> for scientific names or foreign terms, <b> for keywords that should stand out without being more important.

Note: a common mistake is reaching for <strong> just to get bold text and then resetting font-weight: normal — screen readers still announce the emphasis that sighted users cannot see. For pure weight, style a <span>.
